'''Claus Peter Schnorr''' (4 August 1943 – 8 June 2025) was a German mathematician and [[cryptography|cryptographer]].

== Life and career ==
Schnorr received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[Saarland University]] in 1966, and his [[habilitation]] in 1970. Schnorr's contributions to cryptography include his study of [[Schnorr group]]s, which are used in the [[Schnorr signature|digital signature algorithm]] bearing his name. Besides this, Schnorr is known for his contributions to [[algorithmic information theory]] and for creating an approach to the definition of an [[algorithmically random sequence]] which is alternative to the concept of Martin-Löf randomness.<ref name="v802">{{cite book | last=Schnorr | first=Claus Peter | title=Rekursive Funktionen und ihre Komplexität | publisher=Vieweg+Teubner Verlag | publication-place=Wiesbaden | date=1974 | isbn=978-3-519-02322-7 | doi=10.1007/978-3-322-94701-7 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-322-94701-7 | language=de | access-date=26 June 2025 | page=}}</ref>

Schnorr was a professor of mathematics and [[computer science]] at the [[Johann Wolfgang Goethe University of Frankfurt am Main|Johann Wolfgang Goethe University]] at [[Frankfurt]]. He retired in 2011 after working there for 40 years. He was also a Distinguished Associate of [[RSA Security|RSA Laboratories]], and a joint recipient of the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] together with [[Johannes Buchmann]] in 1993. He received, with [[Jean-Jacques Quisquater]], the [[RSA Award for Excellence in Mathematics]] in 2013.

Schnorr held a patent on [[Schnorr signature]]s until February 2010.<ref>{{Cite patent|number=US4995082A|title=Method for identifying subscribers and for generating and verifying electronic signatures in a data exchange system|gdate=1991-02-19|invent1=Schnorr|inventor1-first=Claus P.|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US4995082/en}}</ref> He died on 8 June 2025, at the age of 81.<ref>[https://mittelhessen-gedenkt.de/traueranzeige/claus-peter-schnorr Traueranzeige]. mittelhessen-gedenkt.de, 21 June 2025 (in German). Retrieved 21 June 2025.</ref>
